headline: No access problems found for the AI search crawlers we checked.
summary: No access problems found for the AI search crawlers we checked. robots.txt allows the AI search crawlers. AI training crawlers are allowed too. Allowing a crawler only makes your pages available to it. It does not guarantee that any AI assistant or search engine will index, cite, recommend or rank your site.
confirmed: robots.txt allows OAI-SearchBot (ChatGPT search), PerplexityBot (Perplexity search results), Claude-SearchBot (Claude search) and Applebot (Siri, Spotlight and Safari search) on all audited pages.

AI training crawlers allowed by robots.txt: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended and CCBot. Block them only if you do not want your content used for training; it will not affect the AI search crawlers above.
/ answered HTTP 200 to a normal browser request.
No /llms.txt file. llms.txt is an optional, proposed format. The major AI crawler operators do not document using it, so it is not needed for access.
uncertain: Test requests named as OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, GPTBot, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, ClaudeBot, Googlebot, Applebot, CCBot and Bingbot got the normal page. Real crawlers come from their own IP addresses, so IP-based firewall rules could still treat them differently.

suggestedActions.action: No access problems found for the AI search crawlers we checked. Access is only the first step; to see whether AI assistants actually mention you, measure it with the AI Search Visibility Tracker.
Measure whether ChatGPT, Perplexity and others actually mention your brand: https://apify.com/steadfeed/ai-search-visibility-tracker
